_comment: The one place the screenshot pipeline and the App Store Connect uploader agree on what
Kadō publishes: which languages, which device sizes, and which canvas each size needs.
Scripts/screenshots.sh reads it to know what to photograph; Scripts/appstore.py reads it
Nothing here names App Store Connect's device families. Screenshots go through the App
Asset Library, where each is placed in a *placement group* (IPHONE_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_LARGE_
PROFILE, IPAD_13_PROFILE, …), and appstore.py looks the group up from `size` in Apple's
reference data on every run — Apple adds families there without an API version change, and
a hard-coded name is the thing that goes stale. `Scripts/appstore.py info` prints the groups
the listing holds and warns about any this file would not produce.
iphone-duo is the iPhone Duo's *outer* display, 1398x2034 — the size Apple's
IPHONE_DUO_PROFILE takes beside the inner 2007x2853. Outer because Kadō is laid out for
it already, and because a fresh Duo simulator boots folded, so the capture runs unattended:
nothing in simctl or XCTest can unfold one, and the inner display stays black until a
person does it in Device Hub. Required for builds on the iOS 27.1 SDK from April 2027.
The listing's own locales, not the ones you would guess: English here is en-CA, which is
what App Store Connect actually holds. Writing en-US would not update it — it would add a
second English localization beside it. `Scripts/appstore.py info` prints the live list.
